subject: ERROR: wrong number of arguments in modifier (p1,p1) of element factor1=~pos1

messages.author: ca2bbf3d1fa56ead
messages.subject: ERROR: wrong number of arguments in modifier (p1,p1) of element factor1=~pos1
parts:
Dear colleagues:

I am trying to run a multi-group CFA (2 groups) and ran into the following error.

Codes:

Posfree.model <- 'factor1 =~ c(p1,p1)*pos1 + 
c(p2,p2)*pos3 + c(p3,p3)*gen9 + c(p4,p4)*pos6 +
c(p5,p5)*pos5 + c(p6,p6)*gen1

factor1 ~~ c(1, NA)*factor1

pos1 ~~ c(p101,p101)*pos1
pos3 ~~ c(p102,p102)*pos3
gen9 ~~ c(p103,p103)*gen9
pos6 ~~ c(p104,p104)*pos6
pos5 ~~ c(p105,p105)*pos5
gen1 ~~ c(p106,p106)*gen1

pos5 ~ gen9

pos1 ~ c(p201,p201)*1
pos3 ~ c(p202,p202)*1
gen9 ~ c(p203,p203)*1
pos6 ~ c(p204,p204)*1
pos5 ~ c(p205,p205)*1
gen1 ~ c(p206,p206)*1


factor1 ~ c(0, NA)*1

'


PosfreeFit <- sem(Posfree.model,
                  data = Final_for_analysis, group = "Control", std.lv = TRUE)


summary(PosfreeFit, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized=TRUE)


Error:

Error in lavaanify(model = FLAT, meanstructure = lavoptions$meanstructure,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: wrong number of arguments in modifier (p1,p1) of element factor1=~pos1
In addition: Warning message:
In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
  lavaan WARNING: small number of observations (nobs < nvar)
  nobs = 0 nvar = 6


I have double checked that the group variable "Control" was correctly labeled 1 and 2 for the two groups. 

Would appreciate any comments about what was wrong here. Thanks a ton!

Best

Yun Chen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: ERROR: wrong number of arguments in modifier (p1,p1) of element factor1=~pos1
parts:
lavaan WARNING: small number of observations (nobs < nvar)
  nobs = 0 nvar = 6

I have double checked that the group variable "Control" was correctly labeled 1 and 2 for the two groups.

Given the warning about 0 observations, I wonder whether listwise deletion resulted in trying to fit the model to 1 group instead of 2.  This could happen if all observations in a group are missing at least one variable.  Try setting the argument missing = "fiml" and see what happens (and take care to read up on FIML and its assumptions, if you are unaware).
